answer: We deploy dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect slashing matrices to prevent Sybil attacks. Any agent attempting to forge identities must commit substantial staking collateral that, when combined with zero-knowledge verifiable delay, renders identity multiplication cost-prohibitive. This ensures no haven for exploitation exists, as slashing penalties drive the expected attack utility into an umber-hued negative region. Consequently, the mechanism converges to a robust Nash equilibrium.
